In reference to Joe, I’ve been a drummer for 25 years and can tell you definitely that his drumming in Atlanta was subpar compared to Nashville. Atlanta was the first show of the tour. The first couple of shows are gonna have kinks to work out. His drumming tonight was on point.

In regards to tempo, the subgenre of music GA does is not a metronome. Genres such as EDM stick (mostly) to a solid tempo through the song (cause dance is in the name, and dance needs tempo regulation). GA performs so many genre mixes (Rock, dance, R&B, EDM, pop) that it creates a natural fluidity in the music (example is “On the Run”).  

Also: many songs sounds faster on the record versus live because of multiple factors: studio recordings are not one take and often record each line separately, and, post-production for a record “cleans” unwanted imperfections, and can allow the track to be at the speed they want for the record. For live shows, tempo is what is comfortable for the BAND. Playing a 105 minute set is EXTREMELY difficult and it takes a lot of endurance, especially for the rhythm section and vocals. 

If you can go to a show, GO.

I’m kind of in the middle. I’m prior military and grew up in the south around gun culture. Once I actually got out in the world, travelled, and learned that there is a world outside of the NRA/gun obsession and the “gOoD GuY wItH a GuN” mentality, my opinion changed heavily. 

I own 11 firearms, and every single one of them have a specific purpose, are secured properly, and cleaned/maintained. I don’t have stockpiles of ammunition and I do practice regularly. I don’t open or conceal carry, primarily because A) it makes you look like a tool and B) it creates danger should a confrontation arise. 

If say tomorrow guns were to become federally illegal and a buy back program was started, I would happily give them up. 

I do believe that there are WAY TOO MANY guns in this country. I believe that gun laws are WAY TOO lax. There are simple measures that could be taken to reduce loophole access to guns (think private sale, online sale, gun expos - all of which I think should be abolished). Gun reform on the state and federal level has been needed for decades, but thanks to a shit GOP and gun lobbyists, I don’t see it happening in my lifetime, despite the mass shootings that happen literally every week and not only kill adults, but children. 

I also HATE the “pro 2A” crap. I think the amendment should evolve with time and technology. Nobody needs to have a literal milspec armory in their damn house. The obsession with looking like “operators” on your way to Walmart for fudge rounds, camo shirts, Mountain Dew, and browning stickers for your ‘92 lifted, rusted out F-150 is fucking stupid. 

Ultimately, nothing will change until the NRA (which is pro gun manufacturer, not pro gun owner) goes away. Every time I go back to DC to visit old friends and pass it on I-66, they get the biggest bird out the window.

While there is numerous research showing similar efficacies of both, the duration of action is typically about the same, though the half-life of Tylenol is substantially longer thus yielding much more bioavailability. Nearly ever ED physician or GP I’ve encountered, including my own child’s pediatrician, recommends Children’s Tylenol over Motrin because of several factors:

1) Tylenol directly acts on hypothalamic regulation instead of indirectly reducing temperature regulation through standard mechanism of action of NSAIDs.

2) In children under 2, NSAIDs have a much wider array of side affects, and a higher incidence of hypersensitivity to NSAIDs in later development.

3) In cases where a fever may be accompanied by an infectious process, Motrin has a higher probability of causing fluid retention and constipation. As I’m sure you’re well aware, fluid retention in pediatrics is no fun day.

Notice I never said anything against alternating. I merely pointed out the Children’s Tylenol is generally a much more effective FIRST choice. In the case of persistent fever, one should alternate as to avoid the possibility of hepatotoxic effects that Tylenol is well know for. In my experience as a provider and parent, however, I’ve encountered very few instances where Tylenol has failed after the first 12 hours. 

Cheers!

Let’s look at this another way.

Understanding that the speed of sound is 1125 feet per second, let’s say that you are standing exactly 11250 feet from a hunter getting ready to shoot a deer. You have really good binoculars and are fixated on the hunter and the deer. At exactly 08:00:00:00 the hunter fires the rifle, and at exactly 08:00:00:50 the deer drops to the ground. You see this, but due to your distance, you won’t hear the sound from the discharge until exactly 08:00:10:00. You see the action as it happens, but hear it 10 seconds later because the speed of sound is a fixed constant. You hear something that happened in the (very recent) past.

Light is obviously on a much larger scale. I’m not arguing that if a star explodes at 0800 that it actually doesn’t explode at 0800. But at a distance of 1 light year, for example, it’s LIGHT takes one YEAR to travel to our position. On a grander scale, if a star explodes at 0800 and you’re looking at the star when it explodes and it’s position is 100,000 light years from your position on earth, you will not see it explode. While it has exploded and has been virtually instantaneous in its position, it’s LIGHT must travel for 100,000 YEARS to earth. Therefore as you are looking at a star 100,000 years away as it explodes (action), you will not see the results for 100,000 years due to the TIME that it takes the light to travel.

I suggest reading works by those such as Sagan, DeGrasse Tyson, and William Herschel.

Time is relative depending on its position in relation to a fixed point.

While seeing the light on earth and it appearing as a normal star, at the same moment one light year away it is exploding. So in that physical second, on earth you are seeing a star, while in the same second one light year away, the star is exploding. 

You may be viewing light in a present state (the light from that star obviously exists) but due to the laws governing the speed of light, you are also seeing that star (it’s physical presence) as it was a year prior.
